register: Critical academic and media term for treating technical fixes as sufficient answers to complex political or social problems.
trap: Solutionnisme is not neutral problem-solving: it criticizes the reduction of political choices and structural conflicts to technical problems.
example_tl: Le solutionnisme technologique promet une application pour chaque crise sociale, mais élude les rapports de pouvoir et les responsabilités institutionnelles qui la structurent.
example_en: Technological solutionism promises an app for every social crisis, but evades the power relations and institutional responsibilities that structure it.
cloze: {{c1::Le solutionnisme technologique}} promet une application pour chaque crise sociale, mais élude les rapports de pouvoir et les responsabilités institutionnelles qui la structurent.
note: Old_back is accurate. The card fixes the term’s critical force and records the concise specialist alternative technosolutionnisme.

register: Specialist critical neologism, associated especially with analyses that treat an abstract internet as a single force with its own inherent logic.
trap: This is not political centrism practiced online; it names the habit of putting an abstract idea of the internet at the center of every explanation.
example_tl: L’internet-centrisme de certains réformateurs suppose que la connectivité démocratise mécaniquement la société, alors que les mêmes réseaux peuvent renforcer le contrôle autoritaire.
example_en: The internet-centrism of certain reformers assumes that connectivity automatically democratizes society, whereas the same networks can reinforce authoritarian control.
cloze: {{c1::L’internet-centrisme}} de certains réformateurs suppose que la connectivité démocratise mécaniquement la société, alors que les mêmes réseaux peuvent renforcer le contrôle autoritaire.
note: Materially repairs old_back: the French neologism is hyphenated and written as a single lexical unit, without internal capitalization or spacing. Self-review replaced an abstract possessor with the natural agentive réformateurs.

register: Established critical term in political economy and technology studies for a business logic based on extracting and monetizing behavioral data.
trap: It does not merely denote a market selling surveillance equipment; surveillance describes the system’s method of accumulating and predicting behavior.
example_tl: Le capitalisme de surveillance transforme chaque interaction en matière première comportementale, sans accorder aux usagers de contrôle effectif sur les usages ultérieurs de leurs données.
example_en: Surveillance capitalism turns every interaction into behavioral raw material without granting users effective control over the subsequent uses of their data.
cloze: {{c1::Le capitalisme de surveillance}} transforme chaque interaction en matière première comportementale, sans accorder aux usagers de contrôle effectif sur les usages ultérieurs de leurs données.
note: Old_back gives the established French term but unnecessarily capitalizes its article.

register: Neutral-formal term in research, algorithmic auditing and technology policy; the alternative is more explanatory and less terminological.
trap: Biais may arise from data, design or deployment context; préjugé algorithmique is too anthropomorphic and suggests an intentionally held opinion.
example_tl: Un biais algorithmique peut défavoriser systématiquement les candidates, même lorsque le modèle n’utilise pas le sexe comme variable explicite de décision.
example_en: Algorithmic bias can systematically disadvantage female candidates even when the model does not use sex as an explicit decision variable.
cloze: Un {{c1::biais algorithmique}} peut défavoriser systématiquement les candidates, même lorsque le modèle n’utilise pas le sexe comme variable explicite de décision.
note: Old_back is accurate; the example prevents the mistaken inference that only an explicitly protected variable can generate bias.

register: Established telecommunications-policy term in France; the Net form remains conventional in institutional and journalistic writing.
trap: The term does not claim that online content is politically neutral; it concerns nondiscriminatory treatment of traffic by network access providers.
example_tl: La neutralité du Net interdit à un fournisseur de ralentir un service rival ou de facturer aux plateformes un accès prioritaire à ses abonnés.
example_en: Net neutrality prohibits a provider from slowing a rival service or charging platforms for priority access to its subscribers.
cloze: {{c1::La neutralité du Net}} interdit à un fournisseur de ralentir un service rival ou de facturer aux plateformes un accès prioritaire à ses abonnés.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary initial capitalization; the example anchors the precise regulatory sense. Self-review clarified who charges whom for priority access.

register: Established data-protection and technology-policy term; the en construction is especially natural in France-French institutional prose.
trap: A courtier en données is not any neutral data intermediary: the label usually foregrounds collecting, combining and selling personal profiles.
example_tl: Les courtiers en données combinent des historiques d’achat, des données de localisation et des centres d’intérêt pour vendre des profils rarement consultables ou rectifiables par les personnes concernées.
example_en: Data brokers combine purchase histories, location data, and interests to sell profiles that the people concerned can rarely inspect or correct.
cloze: {{c1::Les courtiers en données}} combinent des historiques d’achat, des données de localisation et des centres d’intérêt pour vendre des profils rarement consultables ou rectifiables par les personnes concernées.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review retained the established plural because the source denotes the industry’s actors, then made the types of brokered data and the access problem more precise.

register: Established media-criticism metaphor for informational isolation attributed specifically to personalized algorithmic selection.
trap: It is not identical to a chambre d’écho: the bubble emphasizes personalized filtering, while the chamber emphasizes mutual reinforcement within a group.
example_tl: Imputer toute la polarisation à la bulle de filtres occulte les conflits sociaux et les campagnes organisées qui nourrissent également les clivages politiques.
example_en: Attributing all polarization to the filter bubble obscures the social conflicts and organized campaigns that also fuel political divisions.
cloze: Imputer toute la polarisation à {{c1::la bulle de filtres}} occulte les conflits sociaux et les campagnes organisées qui nourrissent également les clivages politiques.
note: The exact-duplicate report assigns this item to BIG_TECH_VOCAB. Materially improves old_back: the established term uses plural filtres. Self-review replaced divisions publiques with the idiomatic clivages politiques.

register: Established critical political-economy term; the singular is conventional as a classificatory label, while the plural foregrounds the platform sector.
trap: It denotes an economic formation organized around data, network effects and gatekeeping, not merely capitalism taking place inside one online platform.
example_tl: Le capitalisme de plateforme transfère les risques aux travailleurs et aux fournisseurs, tandis que les intermédiaires contrôlent les données, l’accès et les règles du marché.
example_en: Platform capitalism transfers risks to workers and suppliers while intermediaries control data, access, and market rules.
cloze: {{c1::Le capitalisme de plateforme}} transfère les risques aux travailleurs et aux fournisseurs, tandis que les intermédiaires contrôlent les données, l’accès et les règles du marché.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization. The alternative records the common plural variant without displacing the conventional singular label.

register: Established but often promotional anglicism in innovation discourse; critical prose frequently questions whether the promised rupture is real.
trap: In this domain disruption is not a simple perturbation or service interruption; it claims a radical transformation of a market or institutional model.
example_tl: La disruption promise dans l’éducation a surtout privatisé des ressources publiques et rendu les établissements dépendants de plateformes propriétaires difficiles à quitter.
example_en: The disruption promised in education mainly privatized public resources and made institutions dependent on proprietary platforms that are difficult to leave.
cloze: {{c1::La disruption}} promise dans l’éducation a surtout privatisé des ressources publiques et rendu les établissements dépendants de plateformes propriétaires difficiles à quitter.
note: The exact-duplicate report assigns the digital-economy sense to BIG_TECH_VOCAB. Materially corrects old_back, whose perturbation misses the market-transformation claim.

register: Critical term in postcolonial studies and technology policy for asymmetric control of infrastructure, standards, data and extracted value.
trap: It is stronger than dépendance numérique: it frames infrastructural and data control as a structural relationship of domination and extraction.
example_tl: Le colonialisme numérique s’enracine lorsque des entreprises étrangères contrôlent les données et les infrastructures, tandis que les sociétés locales participent à peine à la définition des règles.
example_en: Digital colonialism takes root when foreign companies control data and infrastructure while local societies barely participate in defining the rules.
cloze: {{c1::Le colonialisme numérique}} s’enracine lorsque des entreprises étrangères contrôlent les données et les infrastructures, tandis que les sociétés locales participent à peine à la définition des règles.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from capitalization; the example fixes the structural domination sense rather than treating every foreign technology purchase as colonialism. Self-review restored the definite articles for natural French parallelism.

register: Ville intelligente is neutral in urban policy; the English loan remains frequent in consulting, municipal promotion and sectoral discourse.
trap: Smart does not translate as astucieuse here and the term is not limited to connectivity; it covers urban management through sensors, data and automation.
example_tl: La ville intelligente perd toute portée démocratique lorsqu’elle achète des capteurs avant de définir des objectifs publics et des limites contraignantes à l’usage des données.
example_en: The smart city loses all democratic substance when it buys sensors before defining public objectives and binding limits on data use.
cloze: {{c1::La ville intelligente}} perd toute portée démocratique lorsqu’elle achète des capteurs avant de définir des objectifs publics et des limites contraignantes à l’usage des données.
note: Old_back is accurate; the English loan is retained only as a marked sectoral alternative.

register: Critical term in intellectual history and technology commentary; the analytical alternative is transparent and slightly more formal.
trap: It is not optimism about one innovation: it attributes to technology the power to lead society toward an ideal order by itself.
example_tl: Le techno-utopisme des années quatre-vingt-dix a sous-estimé la rapidité avec laquelle la publicité, la surveillance et les plateformes fermées transformeraient les réseaux ouverts.
example_en: The techno-utopianism of the 1990s underestimated how quickly advertising, surveillance, and closed platforms would transform open networks.
cloze: {{c1::Le techno-utopisme}} des années quatre-vingt-dix a sous-estimé la rapidité avec laquelle la publicité, la surveillance et les plateformes fermées transformeraient les réseaux ouverts.
note: Old_back identifies the correct lexeme but omits the article and unnecessarily capitalizes the common noun. Self-review restored articles in the coordinated subject for idiomatic prose.

register: Specialist social-science term; datafication is established in research, while mise en données is a transparent French analytical alternative.
trap: Datafication is not synonymous with numérisation: it specifically turns activities, relationships or qualities into quantifiable, processable data.
example_tl: La datafication de l’école modifie non seulement son administration, mais aussi les critères selon lesquels sont évalués les résultats, les comportements et les besoins d’accompagnement.
example_en: The datafication of schools changes not only their administration but also the criteria by which results, behavior, and support needs are assessed.
cloze: {{c1::La datafication}} de l’école modifie non seulement son administration, mais aussi les critères selon lesquels sont évalués les résultats, les comportements et les besoins d’accompagnement.
note: The exact-duplicate report assigns this item to BIG_TECH_VOCAB. Old_back supplies the accepted loan but incorrectly capitalizes the common noun. Self-review restored the articles before the coordinated evaluation targets.

tl: le paradoxe de la vie privée
register: Established behavioral-research and data-protection term for the apparent gap between stated privacy concern and observable disclosure behavior.
trap: The gap between stated concern and observed behavior does not prove indifference: platform design and a lack of alternatives constrain meaningful choice.
example_tl: Le paradoxe de la vie privée ne prouve pas que les usagers soient incohérents, puisque les interfaces manipulatrices et l’absence d’alternatives limitent leur capacité réelle de choisir.
example_en: The privacy paradox does not prove that users are inconsistent, since manipulative interfaces and the absence of alternatives limit their real ability to choose.
cloze: {{c1::Le paradoxe de la vie privée}} ne prouve pas que les usagers soient incohérents, puisque les interfaces manipulatrices et l’absence d’alternatives limitent leur capacité réelle de choisir.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review framed the example cautiously so the research label is not mistaken for a causal explanation, improved the final collocation, and removed a narrower confidentiality alternative.

register: Common journalistic and lifestyle label in France French; the full alternative is transparent but more clinical and less idiomatic in everyday media usage.
trap: It must not be confused with the droit à la déconnexion, the employment-law protection concerning work communications outside working hours.
example_tl: La détox numérique promet un soulagement individuel, mais ne modifie pas les modèles économiques qui transforment chaque minute passée hors ligne en manque à gagner.
example_en: Digital detox promises individual relief but does not change the business models that turn every minute spent offline into lost revenue.
cloze: {{c1::La détox numérique}} promet un soulagement individuel, mais ne modifie pas les modèles économiques qui transforment chaque minute passée hors ligne en manque à gagner.
note: Materially reorders old_back: désintoxication numérique is understandable, but détox numérique is the more idiomatic France-French production label. Self-review replaced a translated attention perdue metaphor with the natural manque à gagner.

register: Established media-economics and technology-criticism term for markets that capture, measure and monetize a scarce cognitive resource.
trap: It does not describe personal time management or an attentive economy; it names a system in which human attention becomes a commodity.
example_tl: L’économie de l’attention récompense davantage l’indignation immédiate que l’analyse rigoureuse, car les plateformes mesurent et monétisent plus facilement les réactions rapides.
example_en: The attention economy rewards immediate outrage more than rigorous analysis because platforms can measure and monetize rapid reactions more easily.
cloze: {{c1::L’économie de l’attention}} récompense davantage l’indignation immédiate que l’analyse rigoureuse, car les plateformes mesurent et monétisent plus facilement les réactions rapides.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization; the contextual sentence fixes the specialist political-economic sense. Self-review replaced vendent with the more precise monétisent.

register: Standard public-policy and inequality-studies term; depending on context, it covers access, affordability, skills, service quality and outcomes.
trap: It is not limited to having an internet connection; equipment, usable speeds, skills and the ability to obtain essential services also matter.
example_tl: La fracture numérique persiste lorsque les foyers sont théoriquement raccordés, mais disposent d’équipements obsolètes, de débits insuffisants ou de services publics inaccessibles.
example_en: The digital divide persists when households are theoretically connected but have obsolete equipment, inadequate speeds, or inaccessible public services.
cloze: {{c1::La fracture numérique}} persiste lorsque les foyers sont théoriquement raccordés, mais disposent d’équipements obsolètes, de débits insuffisants ou de services publics inaccessibles.
note: The exact-duplicate report assigns this item to BIG_TECH_VOCAB. Old_back is accurate; the example prevents a narrow coverage-only reading.

register: Emerging critical term in geopolitics and technology policy; the paraphrastic alternative is more transparent in general prose.
trap: It is broader than surveillance alone: it concerns the use of digital infrastructures, automated decisions and information control to consolidate authoritarian power.
example_tl: Le techno-autoritarisme associe surveillance massive, censure automatisée et contrôle des infrastructures afin de rendre la contestation politique plus visible et plus coûteuse.
example_en: Techno-authoritarianism combines mass surveillance, automated censorship, and infrastructure control to make political dissent more visible and more costly.
cloze: {{c1::Le techno-autoritarisme}} associe surveillance massive, censure automatisée et contrôle des infrastructures afin de rendre la contestation politique plus visible et plus coûteuse.
note: Old_back identifies the intended neologism but omits the article and capitalizes it unnecessarily.

register: Established privacy and digital-citizenship term for the accumulated records, inferred attributes and traces associated with a person’s digital activity.
trap: Empreinte numérique can also denote technology’s environmental footprint; in privacy contexts it includes passively collected and inferred data, not only deliberate posts.
example_tl: L’empreinte numérique d’une personne comprend des recherches, des déplacements et des métadonnées que des entreprises conservent même lorsqu’elle n’a jamais publié ces informations.
example_en: A person’s digital footprint includes searches, movements, and metadata that companies retain even when that person has never published that information.
cloze: {{c1::L’empreinte numérique}} d’une personne comprend des recherches, des déplacements et des métadonnées que des entreprises conservent même lorsqu’elle n’a jamais publié ces informations.
note: The exact-duplicate report assigns this item to BIG_TECH_VOCAB. Old_back is accurate; the trap records the genuine environmental ambiguity. Self-review restored the articles and removed a number-sensitive alternative.

register: Integrated institutional and policy term; masculine singular big data remains dominant in many technical and business settings in France.
trap: Do not calque the English adjective as grandes données; mégadonnées is plural, whereas the loan le big data normally takes singular agreement.
example_tl: Les mégadonnées permettent de repérer des tendances à grande échelle, mais leur volume ne corrige ni les échantillons biaisés ni les catégories construites selon des critères discriminatoires.
example_en: Big data makes it possible to identify large-scale trends, but its volume corrects neither biased samples nor categories built using discriminatory criteria.
cloze: {{c1::Les mégadonnées}} permettent de repérer des tendances à grande échelle, mais leur volume ne corrige ni les échantillons biaisés ni les catégories construites selon des critères discriminatoires.
note: Materially improves the unchanged English old_back by supplying the integrated French term and its required plural agreement. Self-review clarified that the category design, rather than the categories themselves, rests on discriminatory criteria.

register: Cloud computing is the dominant neutral technical term in France French; informatique en nuage is an institutional or explanatory alternative.
trap: Le cloud may name the remote environment or service offering, while cloud computing names the computing model; infonuagique is associated mainly with Canadian French.
example_tl: Le cloud computing réduit les coûts initiaux, mais enferme parfois les administrations dans des contrats opaques et les soumet à des juridictions étrangères.
example_en: Cloud computing reduces upfront costs but sometimes locks government agencies into opaque contracts and subjects them to foreign jurisdictions.
cloze: {{c1::Le cloud computing}} réduit les coûts initiaux, mais enferme parfois les administrations dans des contrats opaques et les soumet à des juridictions étrangères.
note: Materially reorders old_back: informatique en nuage is valid but marked, while the English loan is the usual production term in France. Self-review made administrations the contractual party and replaced an abstract dependency phrase with the precise jurisdictional risk.

register: Established interdisciplinary digital-policy concept; the singular construction is compact and classificatory, while the plural is natural in discursive prose.
trap: It is broader than réglementation des plateformes: it also includes private rules, design, moderation, appeals and participation by multiple actors.
example_tl: La gouvernance des plateformes ne se réduit pas au retrait de contenus, puisqu’elle détermine aussi qui fixe les règles et comment contester une décision.
example_en: Platform governance is not limited to content removal, since it also determines who sets the rules and how a decision can be challenged.
cloze: {{c1::La gouvernance des plateformes}} ne se réduit pas au retrait de contenus, puisqu’elle détermine aussi qui fixe les règles et comment contester une décision.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from its missing article and capitalization; the example supplies the concept’s broader institutional scope.

register: Marked Anglophone journalistic neologism, masculine in French; it benefits from explanation on first mention outside technology-policy circles.
trap: Techlash combines tech and backlash: it denotes a broad public and political reaction against Big Tech power, not a technical failure or one bad news cycle.
example_tl: Le techlash a placé des abus naguère traités comme des incidents isolés au centre du débat sur la concurrence, les données et le pouvoir économique.
example_en: The techlash placed abuses once treated as isolated incidents at the center of debate over competition, data, and economic power.
cloze: {{c1::Le techlash}} a placé des abus naguère traités comme des incidents isolés au centre du débat sur la concurrence, les données et le pouvoir économique.
note: Old_back identifies the loan but unnecessarily capitalizes it; the example fixes its collective backlash sense.

register: Established analytical and media term; the prefixed form is concise, while the transparent alternative fits less specialized prose.
trap: Techno-optimism does not necessarily entail techno-utopianism: confidence in innovation need not claim that technology alone will resolve social conflict.
example_tl: Le techno-optimisme gouvernemental présente l’intelligence artificielle comme un progrès inévitable et relègue ses coûts sociaux et environnementaux au rang d’effets secondaires.
example_en: The government’s techno-optimism presents artificial intelligence as inevitable progress and relegates its social and environmental costs to mere side effects.
cloze: {{c1::Le techno-optimisme}} gouvernemental présente l’intelligence artificielle comme un progrès inévitable et relègue ses coûts sociaux et environnementaux au rang d’effets secondaires.
note: Old_back identifies the correct lexeme but omits the article and unnecessarily capitalizes the common noun.

register: Central but contested technology-policy concept; souveraineté technologique is related but can encompass broader industrial capabilities.
trap: It does not necessarily mean national autarky: it can concern public, collective or individual capacity to decide about data, standards and infrastructure.
example_tl: La souveraineté numérique européenne suppose de pouvoir auditer les systèmes critiques et changer de fournisseur, plutôt que d’interdire toute technologie étrangère.
example_en: European digital sovereignty requires the ability to audit critical systems and change providers rather than banning all foreign technology.
cloze: {{c1::La souveraineté numérique}} européenne suppose de pouvoir auditer les systèmes critiques et changer de fournisseur, plutôt que d’interdire toute technologie étrangère.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from the missing article and unnecessary capitalization; the trap distinguishes strategic capacity from isolation.

alts: la technologie au service de l’intérêt général
register: Emerging professional and academic field without a fully stabilized France-French label; the alternative is explanatory rather than terminological.
trap: Intérêt général does not simply mean popular or state-funded: it orients design, deployment and accountability toward collective needs and rights.
example_tl: La technologie d’intérêt général associe ingénieurs, juristes et citoyens afin que les services numériques protègent effectivement les droits et répondent aux besoins collectifs.
example_en: Public interest technology brings together engineers, lawyers, and citizens so that digital services effectively protect rights and address collective needs.
cloze: {{c1::La technologie d’intérêt général}} associe ingénieurs, juristes et citoyens afin que les services numériques protègent effectivement les droits et répondent aux besoins collectifs.
note: Materially diverges from old_back: intérêt public is understandable, but intérêt général is the idiomatic French public-policy collocation. Terminology remains unsettled, so the explicit paraphrase is retained as an alternative.

register: Culture numérique is natural in France-French education and policy prose; littératie numérique is a more explicit specialist research term.
trap: The concept is not limited to operating devices: it includes evaluating sources, understanding risks, creating content and participating critically and safely.
example_tl: La culture numérique permet de repérer les interfaces manipulatrices et de vérifier les sources, deux compétences aussi nécessaires que la maîtrise de nouvelles applications.
example_en: Digital literacy makes it possible to identify manipulative interfaces and verify sources, two skills as necessary as mastering new applications.
cloze: {{c1::La culture numérique}} permet de repérer les interfaces manipulatrices et de vérifier les sources, deux compétences aussi nécessaires que la maîtrise de nouvelles applications.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review retained the mainstream France-French headword while recording the more exact but specialist littératie label, and clarified the apposition in the example.

register: Standard masculine technical borrowing in France French; as an adjective, open source is postpositive and invariable.
trap: Open source is not identical to logiciel libre: the movements overlap in licensing practice but frame their principles and goals differently.
example_tl: L’open source facilite l’audit indépendant des modèles, mais la publication du code ne garantit ni une communauté active ni une gouvernance transparente.
example_en: Open source facilitates independent auditing of models, but publishing the code guarantees neither an active community nor transparent governance.
cloze: {{c1::L’open source}} facilite l’audit indépendant des modèles, mais la publication du code ne garantit ni une communauté active ni une gouvernance transparente.
note: Old_back leaves the English expression articleless and capitalized; the production headword supplies French nominal syntax and lowercase styling.

register: Neutral technical and political term; web keeps the reference to web services rather than expanding the claim to all internet infrastructure.
trap: Décentralisé does not necessarily mean distribué: infrastructure may be spread across machines while decisive control or governance remains concentrated.
example_tl: Le web décentralisé cherche à réduire la dépendance à l’égard d’un intermédiaire unique, mais ses protocoles peuvent concentrer le pouvoir entre les mains de quelques développeurs.
example_en: The decentralized web seeks to reduce dependence on a single intermediary, but its protocols can concentrate power in the hands of a few developers.
cloze: {{c1::Le web décentralisé}} cherche à réduire la dépendance à l’égard d’un intermédiaire unique, mais ses protocoles peuvent concentrer le pouvoir entre les mains de quelques développeurs.
note: Old_back is accurate apart from unnecessary capitalization; the example avoids equating decentralized architecture with democratic governance. Self-review replaced two translated collocations with idiomatic French constructions.

register: Established umbrella term in media research and European policy; the adjectival alternative is compact and also current.
trap: It is broader than deliberate désinformation: it can also include misinformation and genuine material shared out of context to cause harm.
example_tl: Le désordre de l’information ne découle pas seulement d’informations fabriquées, mais aussi de faux contextes, de contenus manipulés et d’incitations algorithmiques opaques.
example_en: Information disorder arises not only from fabricated information but also from false contexts, manipulated content, and opaque algorithmic incentives.
cloze: {{c1::Le désordre de l’information}} ne découle pas seulement d’informations fabriquées, mais aussi de faux contextes, de contenus manipulés et d’incitations algorithmiques opaques.
note: Old_back identifies the concept but lacks the article and unnecessarily capitalizes it; the preferred form follows established European institutional usage. Self-review removed the ambiguous phrase nouvelles inventées.
